unit: Algebra · Chapter 2. Statistics, combinatorics and probability
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 12 mathematics textbooks (general stream)

stages.headline: The probability of an event is P(A) = m/n, where n counts all equally likely outcomes and m those favourable to A; 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1.
stages.headlineEnglish: The probability of an event is P(A) = m/n, where n counts all equally likely outcomes and m those favourable to A; 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1.

stages.headline: The opposite event has P(not A) = 1 − P(A); for mutually exclusive A and B, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).
stages.headlineEnglish: The opposite event has P(not A) = 1 − P(A); for mutually exclusive A and B, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).

stages.headline: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B); two coins both showing heads: ½ · ½ = ¼.
stages.headlineEnglish: For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B); two coins both showing heads: ½ · ½ = ¼.
